title: Outer multiplication loop
statement: Let $x,a,b$ be bit strings and let $v$ be a register assignment bounded by $4(|x|+1)$ in every register. Suppose $v(4)=v(0)+2|a|$, $v(5)=v(2)+2|b|$, the input bits at positions $v(0)+2p$ and $v(2)+2q$ reproduce respectively the bits of $a$ and $b$ for every $p<|a|$ and $q<|b|$ (with out-of-range bits treated as $0$), and $v(8)+|a|+|b|\le 4(|x|+1)$. Define $S=\sum_{p<|a|}\sum_{q<|b|} [v(7)=v(8)+p+q]a_p b_q$, where bits are identified with $0$ or $1$, and suppose $v(11)+S\le 4(|x|+1)$. Then there is a final register assignment, still bounded by $4(|x|+1)$, in which registers $0$, $8$, and $11$ equal respectively $v(0)+2|a|$, $v(8)+|a|$, and $v(11)+S$, and every register other than $0,8,9,10,11$ retains its initial value. The fixed multiplication program reaches its result-test state with this assignment and no answer recorded, with all earlier configurations satisfying its instruction side conditions and register bound.
